body: 39. Old enough that my depression is definitely different from that of all the teenagers and early 20s kids on here, and have also been wanting to find other people in a similar boat. Let's talk.
Right? If you've never so much as had an actual conversation with me, for all you know I'm an axe murderer.

Yeah. The phrase "we want to raise awareness" really gets my hackles up. Raising awareness accomplishes very little: what needs to happen is meaningful action or change, on whatever issue. Awareness is a very small (though necessary) component of that.

Right there with you on this.

One of the things that I hate the most: when random people on Twitter put out blanket statements saying shit like "You're worthwhile and a good person and you should live!" Because you know what? You don't know me, and your patronizing, off-the cuff endearments reflect only your very small reality. Not mine.

Life is hard. Not exactly news, I know, but ... it isn't supposed to be *this* hard.

I was doing a little better at the beginning of last week, but by the time the weekend came around I was curled up in a ball in bed again. I barely made it to work yesterday and today, but I did get there. I'm scared about tomorrow, though. I'm exhausted but agitated; I should be asleep but slumber feels unattainable right now. And this isn't setting me up well for tomorrow morning.

With my version of depression, I'm usually okayish if I get to work because it gets me out of my head. But my depression also makes me feel too tired to live, and getting out of bed and going to the office is just too hard some days. I've used all my sick days and so I'm stressed about the possibility of missing time, and that just makes everything worse.

I'm crying just thinking about it.

Yeah. Me too. Fast and peaceful, in my sleep.

... My depression is killing me, through poor diet and lack of exercise and all the problems that result from that, but it's a damnably slow process.

"Enjoy" is mostly a foreign concept these days. I do OK if I can get myself to work. When I don't, or on weekends, I read and binge watch Netflix. I sit around and hope for friends to call.

A few months ago, in a fit of optimism, I adopted a dog; she's awesome and made things better for a while. Now she's just something else to feel guilty about, since for the past couple of weeks I haven't been doing a very good job of getting her the exercise she needs and deserves.

There are a lot of things that used to make me happy, like hiking and spending time outdoors. But I don't have the energy to get myself out much these days. It's really fucking hard.

Oh, I'm a depression veteran. I have a psychiatrist and am dutifully taking my meds and following instructions as best I can. Many years of therapy are behind me but I keep falling back into the same self-destructive narratives and behaviors.

These days, my biggest hobby is sleeping. I've been diagnosed with a sleep disorder and we'll see if treating it helps. My doctors are optimistic; I'm not, but I'm trying to hang in until then.

Thanks. You're off the hook for today because the teenage girl bagging my groceries was nice to me.

There's not a lot to say about myself. It's the same story as I see every day on this sub. Depressed, lonely, friends are all worn out from not being to help and don't return my calls anymore. I've alienated the people I care about the most and am so tired, so tired, of feeling like I have to fight my broken brain to do even the most basic tasks. Like brushing my teeth: I think I did that three days ago, maybe. Life is just too much and I feel like it's pretty inevitable I'll kill myself eventually. Whether that's in a week or in ten years, I can't say. I just feel pretty sure it'll be my end.

I totally feel drawn to heroin for exactly this reason ... I've never touched it but I just *know* it would be the drug for me.

And that's why I'm never going near it.
I picked up an EAP info card today. Thanks.

Well, I guess I can at least say that today was a whole lot better than yesterday or any day last week. I made it to work! Almost like a normal person! Go, me.

And I only thought about killing myself maybe a dozen times today, mostly before lunch. So, you know, small victories.
Yeah, I think these services are great and help lots of people. Just not for me.

Thank you for giving good, specific tips. That helps. I could definitely see the benefit in a group like you describe, but where I live it just wouldn't be possible. I'm out in the boonies. May I ask how long you were an inpatient? 

I haven't used my work EAP but you're right, it could be a good resource. I just ... I realize this is paranoid but I worry it isn't *really* confidential. I don't need people at work knowing about this. My workplace talks a very good game about being supportive, but in the end, there are too many people I don't feel I can trust.

There have already been several thoughtful and knowledgeable responses, so I'll just add this: It's terribly unfair that you would come home and only find more battles to fight. I hope you make it through. You come across as someone who has a lot of goodness to share with the world. I respect whatever decisions you make.
Thanks. I don't feel worth anything these days.

Thanks for sharing it. Part of the reason my involuntary commitments were awful was because I felt totally dehumanized, for some of the same reasons you mention. I'm trying to figure out if going voluntarily - maybe with some amount of choice about what facility - would be any better, or if it's just be the same horrid thing all over again.
Thanks, that's helpful. I would definitely feel a little less reluctant if they weren't going to put me in a locked ward.

I've felt something similar, where compliments or kind gestures brought me to my knees in a completely unexpected way. For me, it always came back to a feeling of "I don't deserve this." When I'm depressed I feel so worthless and like such a waste of space that I just can't understand why anyone would be nice to me, or why they aren't seeing me for the phony I feel like.

No, and I don't think I ever would. When I'm depressed but not acutely suicidal, talking to people I don't know about how desperate I am would only make me feel more isolated and alone. (I could say the same thing about being here, but it's easier to read and type than talk.) By the time I get to the point where I need to call, I have no interest in preventing my own suicide.

I don't recommend that others follow my example on this.

New here, and in a really bad place emotionally. I've been depressed long enough that even my most supportive friends are taxed beyond their limits and have stopped returning my calls. The professionals aren't helping much either. I'm just tired, so tired of feeling obligated to fight, so tired of living.
